Twenty Third Indian Antarctic Expedition
Ministry o f Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 21, pp 305-346
Structural Assessment of Maitri Station at  
Antarctica
Anurag Sinha
Structure & Architecture Department 
Engineering Division, Engineers India Ltd., New Delhi
ABSTRACT
National Centre for Antarctic & Ocean Research (NCAOR) invited Engineers India 
Limited (EIL) to associate and participate in the 23r d  Indian Antarctic Expedition (XXIII- 
IAE) for studying the structural adequacy of the Maitri Station that now has over-lived its 
10 year design life by 4 years.
EIL having its headquarters in New Delhi and offices in India and abroad is a premier 
consulting organization in South-east Asia which provides value-added services in varied 
fields of engineering using state-of-the-art technology. During the past EIL has been awarded 
numerous works related to health check of structures including its rehabilitation both in 
India and abroad.
Shri Anurag Sinha (Manager, Structural & Architecture Department, EIL) participated 
in the XXIII-IAE as a summer team member to carry out the assigned project. Shri G 
Veerabhadraiah (Manager, Environment Division, EIL) also participated in the expedition 
to carry out “Review of Waste-water Management System”.
The scope of work for investigation included building comprising the ‘Main Block’, 
‘A Block’, ‘B Block’  and ‘C Block’  of Maitri station.
Necessary data collection was made to study and analyse the present structural 
condition of the station. Major tasks performed during the expedition included compilation 
of the collected data/ information and possible remedial measures covering:
• Detailed visual inspection of the condition of various structural components including 
Columns, Beams, Bracings, Walls, Floor & Roof Panels. The extent of distress and 
damage noted was:
• Existence of longitudinal cracks in some of the main structural columns,
• Sagging of floor panels at certain locations in ‘Main Block’  & ‘B Block’,
• Heavy snow ingress in ‘A Block’  during blizzards.
• Collection of representative samples of structural members (of the stilt), to study 
its metallurgy and confirming its adequacy for usage in the sub-zero conditions.

306 Anurag Sinha
• Videography of the structure to record its present condition and problem areas in 
order to facilitate review at a later date.
• Precautionary measures related to the structure, required to be undertaken 
immediately in order to have less trouble during the preceding long & difficult 
period of winter and darkness were also suggested.
• Collection of information/ feedback from the current occupants (XX-WOT) for 
other noted structural inadequacies and suggestions for planning for future 
requirements.
• Preparation of working sketches in AutoCAD to facilitate easy identification of 
problem areas during subsequent works, and development of detail drawings if 
required for archival purpose.
A report containing observations and recommendations on the subject has already 
been submitted to NCAOR vide document no. 8516-00-16-48-4001 Rev.O dated 15-07- 
2004.
EIL looks forward to actively contribute towards this mission of great importance to 
the nation by offering its services for any engineering and technological requirements.
INTRODUCTION
India started its expeditions to icy continent of Antarctica as early as 
1981 to carry out various scientific research activities. The first permanent 
scientific research station ‘Dakshin Gangotri’  was established in 1983 at 
70° South & 12° East on the ice shelf on Princess Astrid coast of eastern 
Antarctica to provide necessary living and laboratory facilities for the 
wintering over team.
To expand its scientific research program, a second permanent 
scientific station was conceived and a suitable site was selected in 1984 in 
the Schirmacher Oasis region of Central Donning Maud Land of eastern 
Antarctica. A new station named ‘Maitri’  station (refer Figure below) was 
built in the year 1987-88 using indigenous expertise by the Research & 
Development Establishm ent (Engineers) of Defence Research & 
Development Organisation (DRDO). The station was later commissioned 
in 1989 after Dakshin Gangotri got buried under accumulated snow. Winter 
component of the expedition team consisting of 25 members stays in the 
Maitri station for a period of 12 to 15 months.
The active service life of the station was estimated as 10 years at the 
time of its conception, which is now over by 5 years. During this period 
Maitri has withstood the extreme Antarctic weather conditions and served 
as a comfortable shelter for the scientists engaged in Antarctic research.
